expert_root_cause: U3 and R8 footprints were placed too close together during layout, so pads 4 and 1 on the shared SPI_CLK net violate the 0.20mm Default netclass clearance rule.
expert_impact: Increases risk of solder bridging during reflow and raises coupling/crosstalk risk on the SPI_CLK signal, which can cause intermittent communication errors at higher clock rates.
expert_recommendation: Increase spacing between U3 and R8 (reposition components or adjust footprints) to restore at least 0.20mm pad-to-pad clearance; re-run DRC to confirm.

expert_root_cause: The SPI_CLK track segment near U3 was routed narrower (0.12mm) than the minimum qualified track width (0.15mm) for this stackup, likely due to manual routing in a tight area.
expert_impact: Narrow traces are harder to reliably fabricate and can shift characteristic impedance for the high-speed SPI clock signal, risking signal integrity issues.
expert_recommendation: Widen the SPI_CLK track segment to at least 0.15mm, rerouting around the tight area between U3 and R8 if necessary.

expert_root_cause: U3's fabrication/silkscreen text was placed too close to the board edge (Edge.Cuts), violating the 0.15mm silkscreen-to-edge clearance guideline.
expert_impact: Cosmetic/manufacturability issue only: text may be clipped during panel depaneling and become illegible; no direct electrical risk.
expert_recommendation: Move the U3 reference/fabrication text further from the board edge, or reduce text size, to restore the 0.15mm clearance.

expert_root_cause: The SPI_MISO net has two pads (R8 pad 2, R9 pad 1) assigned to the same net but no copper track has been routed between them yet -- the net is incomplete.
expert_impact: The SPI_MISO signal path is not physically connected; the board will not function correctly until this net is routed.
expert_recommendation: Route a track connecting R8 pad 2 and R9 pad 1 on the SPI_MISO net before fabrication.
